title: KV shard LRU: hit-rate vs p95 vs memory sweep and regression harness
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Build a reproducible load-testing harness that sweeps LRU eviction thresholds and number of KV shards to quantify trade-offs between cache hit-rate, p95 generation latency, and memory pressure for the KV prefix cache used in the inference runtime. This ticket captures design, implementation, dashboarding, and automated regression detection so we can continuously validate changes to eviction heuristics and memory accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run deterministic synthetic workloads and recorded production traces at token/sec targets of 5k, 20k, 60k
Produce CSV/JSON outputs with metrics: cache_hit_rate, tokens_per_sec, p95_latency_ms, p50_latency_ms, mem_rss_mb, mem_cache_mb, eviction_rate_per_min
Matrix sweep for [shard_count: 1,2,4,8], [lru_target_fraction: 0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9], [prefetch: off,on] completes within CI job budget and stores artifacts
Grafana dashboard and a perf-checker job that fails CI when p95 regression > +12% or hit_rate drops > 6 percentage points compared to baseline
Automated change detection creates a Linear ticket with a link to the failing run and artifact bundle when thresholds breach
test_plan: 1) Implement harness service that can replay (a) synthetic request generator (Zipf / long-tail prefix distribution) and (b) recorded trace replays from prod-sample S3 bucket. 2) Add runtime flags to control shard_count, lru_fraction, and prefetch toggles. 3) Instrument metrics (Prometheus) and ensure labels include run_id, workload_type, and config. 4) Run full sweep in isolated perf cluster and push artifacts to perf-artifacts/redwood/kvcache/ENG-33488/. 5) Create Grafana dashboard and a nightly job that compares latest baseline to master baseline and triggers regression flow.
steps: Design workload distributions and select 3 representative prefixesets (short, medium, long) — doc: https://go.redwood.design/kvcache/harness-spec
Extend existing load-generator to support token-level pacing and KV-aware trace replay
Expose runtime toggles via env vars and a lightweight REST control endpoint for starting runs
Add Prometheus metrics: kvcache_hit_total, kvcache_miss_total, kvcache_evictions_total, kvcache_memory_bytes, inference_tokens_total, inference_latency_seconds_bucket
Create CI job (perf/sweep-kv-lru) with cacheable artifacts and upload to s3 perf-artifacts
Build Grafana dashboard panels and an alert rule that is evaluated by perf-checker service
Implement perf-checker comparator that computes relative delta to stored baseline and posts to #perf-alerts and creates Linear if thresholds exceeded
results_summary: Initial runs (2024-11-18) against synthetic Zipf workload show: with shard_count=4 and lru_fraction=0.7 we hit tokens/sec=42k, p95=48ms, cache_hit_rate=78%, mem_cache_mb=10240. Lowering fraction to 0.3 raised p95 to 96ms while memory dropped to 4600mb and hit_rate fell to 55%. Prefetch:on improved cold-start hit-rate by ~6pp but increased steady-state eviction churn by 12% leading to slightly higher p95 in some configs. Artifacts uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/redwood/kvcache/ENG-33488/run-20241118-*.tar.gz
